transcript:
This is NPR News now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Stocks are plunging on Wall Street.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is down well over 2 percent this hour after gaining more
than 1,500 points to end the day yesterday.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq is doing worse.
It's down more than 5 percent.
While intelligence companies' stocks are getting pinched, many investors are skittish
about Democratic lawmakers' plans to regulate the AI industry.
Voters across Ohio have sent a clear message they don't want AI data centers in their
communities.
NPR's Andrea Shue reports the issue was on local ballots across the state.
Ohio had by far the most ballot initiatives of any state focused on data centers.
Voters in a dozen and a half communities approved 21 measures that will either keep data centers
out altogether or introduce hurdles to their development.
Attorney Nick Owens is with the grassroots group Conserve Ohio, which backed a number
of the measures.
It's clear when Ohioans are given the choice whether to approve or reject hyperscale data
center developments, they overwhelmingly reject them.
Ohio's Governor-elect Amy Acton has called for a conditional moratorium on new data centers
to ensure they cover their utility costs, meet environmental standards, and are built
with union labor.
Andrea Shue, NPR News.
The size of the Democrats' congressional wins aren't yet known, as not all races have been
called.
NPR's Tamara Keith says two U.S. Senate races are outstanding.
We're still waiting on Senate results from Alaska and Mississippi.
If these races break toward Democrats, that would bring the Democratic majority to 54
plus the two independents who caucus with them.
While this still wouldn't be a filibuster-proof majority, it's a lot of breathing room.
Democrats haven't had that big of a majority in the Senate since they passed the Affordable
Care Act early in the Obama administration.
And PR's Tamara Keith reporting.
The largest airline in the Middle East, Emirates Air, is reporting a sharp drop in earnings.
And PR's Aya Batrawi reports the carrier blames high oil prices and disruptions to travel
because of the war against Iran.
The region's biggest carrier, Emirates Air, recorded profits down 68 percent from the
same six-month period last year.
The Dubai state-backed airline had to furlough some of its staff during the war when flights
were grounded due to Iranian missile and drone strikes on Dubai, including some that hit
the Emirates International Airport and fuel depots.
The company says overall staff numbers have also dropped.
The economy of the United Arab Emirates, particularly the city of Dubai, relies heavily on tourism
and travel.
The erosion of profits by nearly 70 percent is the latest economic marker showing the
impact of the U.S. war on Iran on Gulf nations.
Aya Batrawi and PR News, Dubai.
You're listening to NPR.
Police in Des Moines, Iowa, are telling news outlets there there has been a shooting at
a city post office.
The news outlets in Des Moines, including the Des Moines Register report, multiple people
are said to be injured.
The news outlets report a suspect has been detained.
No other details have been released.
Food conglomerate Kraft Heinz says it is selling off its coffee business in North America.
That includes Maxwell House.
NPR's Alina Seljuk reports the company hopes that the move will help boost growth.
Kraft Heinz has been on deal watch for a while.
Ever since its CEO earlier this year hit pause on a massive breakup the company had planned.
Kraft Heinz had been losing sales and at one point proposed as a solution to undo its historic
merger and split Kraft away from Heinz, dividing faster-growing sauces and condiments from
slower-growing groceries.
But new CEO Steve K. Helene said the real issue was the company under-investing in its
brands.
Now, he's hoping to jumpstart growth in part by selling the majority ownership of its North
American coffee business to a private equity firm called One Rock Capital Partners.
The company did not say how Maxwell or other brands might change.
Alina Seljuk, NPR News.
Weather forecasters say there's been a lot of flash flooding early this morning in parts
of southeastern Tennessee and northern Georgia.
The National Weather Service says the flooding is catastrophic and widespread.
Flood warnings are now up for Polk County, Tennessee, as well as Georgia's Fanon County.
There are reports of evacuations.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News.
So, we'll see you next time.

topics.text: Stocks plunge on Wall Street, with the Nasdaq down more than 5 percent amid AI regulation worries
Ohio voters reject data centers in a dozen and a half communities through 21 local ballot measures
Democratic Senate majority size pending, with Alaska and Mississippi Senate races still uncalled
Emirates Air reports profits down 68 percent as Iran war disrupts Dubai travel and tourism
Police report a shooting at a Des Moines, Iowa post office with multiple injured and a suspect detained
Kraft Heinz to sell majority ownership of its North American coffee business, including Maxwell House, to One Rock Capital
Catastrophic flash flooding hits southeastern Tennessee and northern Georgia, with evacuations and warnings issued
